guide.title: The Pacific Coast Highway from San Francisco to San Diego
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: Six days down the California coast on CA-1 and US-101, through Big Sur, the Central Coast, Santa Barbara and the Los Angeles beaches to San Diego. Big Sur closes for slides at times; check Caltrans first.
sections: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi
Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi
Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi
Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi
Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi
Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Golden Gate Bridge Welcome Center
places.notes: Start on foot at the south end of the bridge for the classic view back over the bay, then follow CA-1 south through the Presidio and Golden Gate Park to the ocean.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Devil's Slide Trail
places.address: Devil's Slide Trail, CA-1, Pacifica, CA 94044
places.notes: A 1.3-mile piece of the old cliffside highway, closed to cars when the tunnels opened in 2013 and now a paved path for walkers and cyclists. Small parking lots at each end.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Sam's Chowder House
places.address: 4210 N Cabrillo Hwy, Half Moon Bay, CA 94019
places.notes: Lobster rolls and chowder at a big roadhouse above the water just north of Half Moon Bay. Ask for the deck when the fog stays offshore.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Duarte's Tavern
places.notes: A family-run tavern in the village of Pescadero since 1894, known for cream of artichoke soup and olallieberry pie. A short detour inland from the coast road.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Pigeon Point Light Station State Historic Park
places.notes: One of the tallest lighthouses on the West Coast. The tower is closed for long-running restoration, but the grounds and cliff overlook are open and good for spotting gray whales in winter and spring.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: HI Pigeon Point Lighthouse Hostel
places.notes: Dorm beds and private rooms in the old keepers' houses next to the lighthouse, run by Hostelling International. About the cheapest sea view on the whole trip; check the hostel's site before you go.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Año Nuevo State Park
places.address: 1 New Years Creek Rd, Pescadero, CA 94060
places.notes: Northern elephant seals breed on these dunes in winter, when access is by guided walk only. The rest of the year a permit hike leads out to the viewing area; check the state park site for reservations.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Natural Bridges State Beach
places.address: 2531 W Cliff Dr, Santa Cruz, CA 95060
places.notes: A sea arch, tide pools at the north end, and a eucalyptus grove where monarch butterflies cluster through the late fall and winter.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Santa Cruz Beach Boardwalk
places.notes: A seaside amusement park running since 1907, with the wooden Giant Dipper coaster and a 1911 Looff carousel. Rides run on a reduced schedule outside summer.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Dream Inn Santa Cruz
places.notes: A tall 1960s hotel set right on Cowell Beach, where every room faces the water and the wharf. Walk to the boardwalk in ten minutes.
places.section: Day 1 · San Francisco to Santa Cruz · 80 mi

places.name: Phil's Fish Market
places.notes: Cioppino and fried fish in a big, casual seafood hall, now in Castroville after many years at Moss Landing harbor. An easy stop where CA-1 meets the artichoke fields.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: Monterey Bay Aquarium
places.notes: Built inside an old sardine cannery at the end of Cannery Row, with a three-story kelp forest and a huge open-ocean tank. Book timed tickets ahead in summer and on holidays.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: Asilomar Hotel & Conference Grounds
places.notes: Julia Morgan designed the first lodges here a century ago. Rooms are plain, but the dunes boardwalk runs straight to the beach and the price is gentle for this coast.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: The Lone Cypress
places.notes: The best-known stop on 17-Mile Drive, the private loop through Pebble Beach that charges a per-car fee at the gates. Bird Rock and Fanshell Overlook along the way are quieter.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: Carmel Mission Basilica
places.notes: Mission San Carlos Borromeo, founded in 1771 and the headquarters of the California missions under Junípero Serra. The museum rooms and gardens take about an hour.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: Cypress Inn
places.notes: A 1929 Mediterranean-style inn in the middle of the village, once co-owned by Doris Day and still openly welcoming to dogs.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: La Bicyclette
places.notes: A small European-style bistro with a wood-fired oven, a short walk from the inns in the village.
places.section: Day 2 · Santa Cruz to Carmel · 45 mi

places.name: Point Lobos State Natural Reserve
places.notes: Granite headlands, cypress groves and coves with harbor seals and sea otters, three miles south of Carmel. Parking inside is limited, so come early.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Bixby Creek Bridge
places.notes: The 1932 concrete arch most people picture when they think of Big Sur. Use the pullout on the north side and keep off the roadway. Highway 1 here closes for slides and storms at times; check Caltrans QuickMap before you set out.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Point Sur State Historic Park
places.address: Point Sur Lighthouse, CA-1, Big Sur, CA 93920
places.notes: An 1889 light station on a volcanic rock above the surf, visited only on guided tours that meet at the gate on Highway 1. Check the state park site for tour days.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Pfeiffer Big Sur State Park
places.notes: Redwoods along the Big Sur River, a short trail to Pfeiffer Falls and a large campground. Reserve campsites well ahead.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Big Sur Lodge
places.notes: Simple cottages inside the state park, with a restaurant and the river trails at the door. The most affordable roof in Big Sur short of a tent.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Glen Oaks Big Sur
places.notes: A restored 1950s motor lodge plus cabins in the redwoods by the river, with gas fireplaces in most rooms.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Big Sur Bakery
places.notes: Wood-fired bread, pastries and breakfast in a house set back from the highway. A good first stop of the morning.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Pfeiffer Beach
places.address: Sycamore Canyon Rd, Big Sur, CA 93920
places.notes: Purple-streaked sand and the arch at Keyhole Rock, at the end of a narrow, unsigned road off Highway 1. The lot is small and charges a day-use fee; RVs and trailers can't make the turns.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Nepenthe
places.notes: A family-run terrace restaurant 800 feet above the coast since 1949. Come for a late lunch and the long view south.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Post Ranch Inn
places.notes: The splurge: tree houses and cliff-edge rooms built into the ridge, adults only.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: McWay Falls
places.address: Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park, 52801 CA-1, Big Sur, CA 93920
places.notes: An 80-foot waterfall pouring onto a beach in Julia Pfeiffer Burns State Park. The overlook trail from the park lot is short and flat; the beach itself is off limits.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Piedras Blancas Elephant Seal Rookery
places.address: Elephant Seal Vista Point, CA-1, San Simeon, CA 93452
places.notes: Thousands of elephant seals haul out on the beach below a free boardwalk, and each season brings something different: births, molting, sparring. Volunteer docents are often on hand.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Moonstone Beach Boardwalk
places.notes: A mile-long boardwalk along the bluffs at Cambria's west edge, with sea otters in the kelp and a good spot to watch the sun go down.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Cambria Pines Lodge
places.notes: A rambling lodge in the pines above town, with big gardens, fireplace rooms and live music in the lounge most nights.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Linn's Restaurant
places.notes: Pot pies, comfort plates and olallieberry pie from a family that started with a farm stand outside town.
places.section: Day 3 · Carmel through Big Sur to Cambria · 100 mi

places.name: Hearst Castle
places.address: 750 Hearst Castle Rd, San Simeon, CA 93452
places.notes: William Randolph Hearst's hilltop estate, now a state historic park, ten miles back up the coast from Cambria. All visits are by guided tour from the visitor center; book on the official site, especially in summer.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Morro Rock
places.notes: A 576-foot volcanic plug at the harbor mouth, protected for nesting peregrine falcons. No climbing; walk the beach on its north side instead.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Giovanni's Fish Market & Galley
places.notes: Fish and chips and clam chowder ordered at the counter and eaten on the waterfront, with sea lions barking from the docks.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Mission San Luis Obispo de Tolosa
places.address: 751 Palm St, San Luis Obispo, CA 93401
places.notes: Founded in 1772, the mission faces a plaza on San Luis Obispo Creek at the edge of downtown. The creekside walk leads to the shops on Higuera Street.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Firestone Grill
places.address: 1001 Higuera St, San Luis Obispo, CA 93401
places.notes: A loud, busy downtown spot for the tri-tip sandwich, the Central Coast's signature cut.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Madonna Inn
places.address: 100 Madonna Rd, San Luis Obispo, CA 93405
places.notes: A 1958 roadside hotel where every room has its own theme, plus pink dining rooms and a famous cake case. Stop for a slice even if you are not staying.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Old Mission Santa Barbara
places.notes: The twin-towered mission above town, with a self-guided tour through the museum, cemetery and gardens. The rose garden across the street is free.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Santa Barbara County Courthouse
places.notes: A 1929 Spanish Colonial Revival courthouse with painted ceilings and tiled stairways. Ride up to the clock tower for the view over the red roofs.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: La Super-Rica Taqueria
places.address: 622 N Milpas St, Santa Barbara, CA 93103
places.notes: A small taqueria with handmade tortillas and a short menu on the wall. Expect a line and a patio seat.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Hotel Californian
places.notes: A Moorish-style hotel at the foot of State Street, a block from the beach and close to the Funk Zone's tasting rooms.
places.section: Day 4 · Cambria to Santa Barbara · 135 mi

places.name: Neptune's Net
places.notes: A roadside seafood shack at the county line, where surfers and motorcyclists share picnic tables over fried shrimp and steamed crab.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: El Matador State Beach
places.notes: Sea stacks and caves at a small cove below the bluffs, reached by a steep trail and stairs from the lot. Best at low tide.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: Getty Villa
places.address: 17985 Pacific Coast Hwy, Pacific Palisades, CA 90272
places.notes: Greek, Roman and Etruscan antiquities in a re-created Roman country house with gardens above the coast. Admission is free with a timed reservation from the Getty's site.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: Santa Monica Pier
places.address: 200 Santa Monica Pier, Santa Monica, CA 90401
places.notes: The 1909 pier with an amusement park, a Ferris wheel over the water and a 1922 carousel. It also marks the western end of Route 66.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: Venice Canals
places.notes: A quiet grid of footpaths and small bridges along the canals Abbot Kinney dug in 1905, two blocks from the noise of the boardwalk.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: Gjusta
places.notes: A bakery and deli in a converted warehouse with breads, smoked fish and breakfast plates. Order at the counter and find a seat on the back patio.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: Hotel Erwin
places.notes: A mid-range hotel right off the boardwalk, with a rooftop bar that looks over the beach.
places.section: Day 5 · Santa Barbara to Venice · 100 mi

places.name: The Queen Mary
places.notes: The 1936 ocean liner, moored in Long Beach for good, with original cabins as hotel rooms and decks to explore on a day visit.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Crystal Cove State Park
places.address: 8471 N Coast Hwy, Laguna Beach, CA 92651
places.notes: Three miles of beach and tide pools plus a historic district of 1930s beach cottages, some of which rent overnight. Cottage booking opens months ahead; check the official site.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Beachcomber at Crystal Cove
places.notes: Breakfast or a sunset drink on a deck right above the sand, in one of the restored cottages of the historic district.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Heisler Park
places.notes: A cliff-top park with gardens, benches and stairways down to small coves and tide pools on Laguna's north end.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: The Ranch at Laguna Beach
places.notes: A ranch-style resort in a canyon just across the highway from the beach, with its own nine-hole golf course.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Torrey Pines State Natural Reserve
places.address: 12600 N Torrey Pines Rd, La Jolla, CA 92037
places.notes: Sandstone bluffs and the rare Torrey pine on short trails above the beach. Park at the beach lot and walk up, or drive to the lodge at the top when spaces allow.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: La Jolla Cove
places.notes: A small cove below the village where sea lions and harbor seals sprawl on the rocks. Snorkelers come for the garibaldi in the marine reserve.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Point Loma Seafoods
places.notes: A fish market and counter at the sportfishing docks since 1963. Get a fish sandwich and eat outside watching the boats.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Cabrillo National Monument
places.address: 1800 Cabrillo Memorial Dr, San Diego, CA 92106
places.notes: The tip of Point Loma, with an 1855 lighthouse, views across the bay to downtown, and tide pools on the west side at low tide.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Balboa Park
places.notes: Spanish Revival buildings from the 1915 exposition, museums, gardens and the botanical building along El Prado. Free to walk around; museums charge separately.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi

places.name: Hotel del Coronado
places.notes: The red-roofed 1888 Victorian resort on Coronado's beach, a fitting last night at the end of the coast road.
places.section: Day 6 · Venice to San Diego · 135 mi
